title: The Shreveport trip with Chet Atkins
summary: Asked about country players, he recalls driving to Shreveport to play with Chet Atkins around 1955-56, the only job he made real money on.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you ever know any country blues players? Any pickers or anything like that? Any bottleneck players? Like I said, I met a lot of them. Chad Atkins. I don't know whether you call him a country man. I hear. He's good, man. He's a really good guitar player.

Wow. You was with me on that trip when I went to play with Chad Atkins. I think we were up there in Shreveport. We drove up there. Alexander. We drove up there. And that's the only job I ever made any money on, to tell you the truth about it.
Really? When was that? When was that?
When that was? When that was?
Well, that was around 55, 56. Somewhere in the house.
Yeah, that was four passes on. That's 11 years ago. That was four passes on. Yeah. Yeah. 11 years ago.

I mean they offered me a hundred dollars a night, free rent. Ain't no food or nothing to buy. And I got that. No cutting corners or changing the situation when I got there. And I did get more nights than what they offered me. Oh, that's good. Yeah. Everybody enjoyed it so well, you know. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
